findings.reason: the assertion must cover the key set the deliverable keeps, otherwise the node is closable on a partial fix of the very flicker it was dispatched for.
findings.text: §10's first done-when asserts that only "the schedule, sprints, endpoints and ready set" are never empty, while the deliverable at line 236 requires every block `derivedBlocks` returns plus the milestones and north stars and the "why" names the timeline, milestones and north stars as emptied by the same path, so a fix that keeps those four keys and still blanks the rest turns this gate green while the symptom the lead reported ("everything below it jumped") survives

findings.reason: the fleet-event half of §11's deliverable is its main behavioural change, and without a control asserting the old refresh the node cannot show the guard it adds is the thing that suppressed it.
findings.text: §11's loader case asserts the absence of a refresh within the settle window on a `fleet` event with no positive control showing the pre-change code refreshed on that event, so the control that would discriminate the change is only the poll case's (which is about a different behaviour), and an absence assertion holds equally when the refetch machinery is broken or the listener never receives the event
